title: Software defined radio and DSP
blurb: Explain how an SDR samples and processes signals: Nyquist, aliasing, bit depth, FIR filters, SSB generation and the FFT.

E7F01.why: **Direct sampling** digitizes the incoming RF with an ADC **without mixing** it with a local oscillator first.
E7F01.trap: I and Q generation and switching mixers are other receiver styles.

E7F02.why: An **adaptive filter** learns the noise and removes it from received SSB audio.
E7F02.trap: A crystal-lattice filter is analog. A Hilbert filter is used to generate SSB.

E7F03.why: A **Hilbert-transform filter** makes the 90° shifted copy of the audio needed to generate SSB.
E7F03.trap: Adaptive filters remove noise; notch filters remove one tone.

E7F04.why: Combine the audio and its 90° copy, mixed with quadrature carriers: **signals combined in quadrature phase**. One sideband adds, the other cancels.

E7F05.why: Sample at **at least twice** the highest frequency (Nyquist): 2 kHz audio needs 4 kS/s or more.
E7F05.trap: Half the rate or equal rate would alias the signal.

E7F06.why: 1 V ÷ 1 mV = 1000 levels. 2⁹ = 512 is too few, 2¹⁰ = 1024 is enough: **10 bits**.

E7F07.why: The **FFT** converts a signal from the **time domain to the frequency domain**: a waveform becomes a spectrum.
E7F07.trap: ADCs and DACs convert analog and digital, not time and frequency.

E7F08.why: **Decimation** lowers the effective sample rate by **removing samples**, such as keeping every 4th.
E7F08.trap: It isn't decimal or BCD conversion, and it doesn't attenuate the signal.

E7F09.why: After decimation the Nyquist limit is lower. The filter **removes high frequencies that would otherwise fold down as lower-frequency aliases**.

E7F10.why: A direct-sampling SDR can only see up to half the **sample rate**, so that sets the maximum bandwidth.
E7F10.trap: Bit width sets signal level resolution, not bandwidth.

E7F11.why: The smallest step is **reference voltage ÷ 2ⁿ**. Reference voltage and **sample width in bits** set the minimum detectable signal.
E7F11.trap: Jitter and phase noise affect quality, not the smallest step.

E7F12.why: A FIR filter with symmetric taps can **delay every frequency component by the same amount**, so it does not smear the waveform.
E7F12.trap: FIR is not easier for a given rolloff: sharp ones need many taps.

E7F13.why: Taps **provide incremental delays**: each tap is one more delayed copy of the signal for the algorithm.
E7F13.trap: Taps have nothing to do with debugging access or baseband generation.

E7F14.why: **More taps** give the filter more points to shape its response, so the slope is sharper.
E7F14.trap: A higher data rate or double-precision math doesn't sharpen the shape.
